subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Which of this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 should be the single canonical fix for the exec-approvals VirtioFS lock leak?
rationale: Both branches target the same authorization-store owner boundary, but they differ in hardening and proof presentation; accepting either is a security and maintenance decision rather than a safe mechanical merge choice.

options.title: Adopt this PR after live proof
options.body: Select this branch as canonical only after its author supplies redacted exact-head VirtioFS runtime evidence and the owner approves its larger local lock protocol.

options.title: Adopt the prior live-proven path
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 as the canonical baseline, then port only independently justified hardening from this branch.

options.title: Pause for shared-lock direction
options.body: Defer both branches until maintainers decide whether the corrected sidecar-lock protocol should be released through `@openclaw/fs-safe` instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt the prior live-proven path
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 as the canonical baseline, then port only independently justified hardening from this branch.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the production reproduction and own the overlapping implementation that must be compared before one branch is selected.
